blocks.text: Assalam-o-alaikum bachon! Aaj se hum Unit 1 shuru kar rahe hain: Complex Numbers. Is sabaq mein hum yeh seekhenge ke complex numbers kya hain, yeh kyun banaye gaye, aur in ki shakal kaisi hoti hai. Pichli classon mein aap ne natural numbers, integers, fractions aur real numbers parhe the; aaj hum dekhenge ke number system ko ek qadam aur aage kyun barhana para.

Sab se pehle ek kahani suniye. Insaan ne "number" ka tasawwur (idea) ek dum se nahi banaya; jab bhi koi nayi zaroorat aayi, number system ko thora sa barha diya gaya. Kitab yahan ek mashhoor kahawat yaad dilati hai: "Necessity is the mother of invention", yani zaroorat ijaad ki maan hai. Shuru mein sirf ginti wale numbers the: 1, 2, 3, ... Phir qarz aur nuqsan likhne ki zaroorat pari to negative numbers aaye. Roti ke hisse karne ki zaroorat pari to rational numbers (fractions) aaye. Phir pata chala ke square ka diagonal \(\sqrt{2}\) kisi fraction se poora nahi likha ja sakta, to irrational numbers aaye. Har dafa sawal pehle aaya, aur naya number baad mein.

Ab yahan ruk kar sochiye: \(3^2 = 9\) aur \((-3)^2 = 9\). Positive number ka square bhi positive aur negative number ka square bhi positive. Zero ka square zero. Yani koi bhi real number aisa nahi jis ka square negative ho. Is ka seedha nateeja yeh hai ke \(\sqrt{-1}\), \(\sqrt{-4}\) jaise numbers real numbers ki duniya mein mojood hi nahi. Isi liye sadiyon tak mathematicians ne negative numbers ke square roots ko nazar-andaz kiya, jaise koi bekaar cheez ho. Lekin baad ke daur mein in par tafseel se kaam hua aur yeh numbers pure, applied, financial aur computational mathematics ki bohat si shakhon mein bare kaam ke saabit hue.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Kya koi real number \(x\) aisa hai jis ke liye \(x^2 = -9\) ho? Thora ruk kar sochiye, phir aage parhiye. Jawab: nahi, kyunke \(x\) positive ho, negative ho ya zero, \(x^2\) kabhi negative nahi hota. Yahi woh "zaroorat" hai jis ne complex numbers ko janam diya.

Ab definition dhyan se parhiye, kyunke poori unit isi par khari hai. Jo numbers \(z = a + ib\) ki shakal mein hon, jahan \(a\) aur \(b\) real numbers hon (\(a, b \in \mathbb{R}\)) aur \(i = \sqrt{-1}\) ho, unhein complex numbers kehte hain. Misaal ke taur par \(3 + 4i\), \(2 - \frac{5}{7}i\) aur \(-7 - 2i\) sab complex numbers hain. In tamam numbers ke set (majmooe) ko \(C\) se likhte hain.

blocks.latex: z = a + ib,\quad a, b \in \mathbb{R},\quad i = \sqrt{-1}
blocks.text_alt: z equals a plus i b, where a and b are real numbers and i is the square root of minus one

blocks.text: Is definition ke teen hisse alag alag samajh lein. Pehla, \(a\) ek aam real number hai jo akela khara hai. Doosra, \(b\) bhi ek aam real number hai, lekin is ke saath \(i\) juda hua hai. Teesra, \(i\) woh naya number hai jis ka square \(-1\) hai. Yani complex number koi "ajeeb" cheez nahi; yeh do purane, jaane pehchane real numbers ka ek jora hai, jinhein \(i\) ki madad se ek saath likha gaya hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(a, b \in \mathbb{R}\) ko aise parhiye: "\(a\) aur \(b\) real numbers ke set mein shamil hain". Symbol \(\in\) ka matlab hai "ka hissa hai / mein shamil hai".
Ab kitab ki teen misalon mein \(a\) aur \(b\) pehchante hain:
\(3 + 4i\) mein: \(a = 3\) aur \(b = 4\).
\(2 - \frac{5}{7}i\) mein: \(a = 2\) aur \(b = -\frac{5}{7}\). Dekhiye, minus ka sign \(b\) ke saath jata hai, kyunke \(2 - \frac{5}{7}i\) asal mein \(2 + \left(-\frac{5}{7}\right)i\) hai.
\(-7 - 2i\) mein: \(a = -7\) aur \(b = -2\).
\(i\) ki zaroorat kyun pari? Equation \(x^2 = -1\) ka koi real hal nahi, kyunke har real number ka square \(\ge 0\) hota hai. To mathematicians ne kaha: chaliye ek naya number maan lete hain, naam rakhte hain \(i\), aur us ki pehchan yeh hai ke \(i^2 = -1\). Baqi saare complex numbers isi \(i\) se bante hain. Bilkul aise jaise kisi mistri ke paas naya ozaar (tool) aa jaye jo woh kaam kar de jo purane ozaaron se mumkin hi nahi tha.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh misaal kitab ki nahi, hamari taraf se hai. Equation \(x^2 + 4 = 0\) lijiye. Is ka matlab \(x^2 = -4\). Real numbers mein koi jawab nahi. Lekin \(i\) ke saath:
\[(2i)^2 = 4i^2\]
\[= 4(-1) = -4\]
Yani \(x = 2i\) is equation ko poora karta hai, aur isi tarah \(x = -2i\) bhi. Dekha aap ne? Jo sawal pehle "namumkin" tha, \(i\) ne us ka jawab de diya.

blocks.title: About this unit
blocks.text:
Yeh unit kis baare mein hai: real numbers ek bohat seedhe sawal ka jawab nahi de sakte: "woh kaun sa number hai jis ka square \(-1\) ho?" Is unit mein hum ek bara number system banate hain, complex numbers \(a + ib\), jis mein aise sawalon ka jawab hamesha mil jata hai.
Aap kya seekhenge: real part, imaginary part aur conjugate (jora / ulta sign wala saathi); complex numbers ko jama, tafreeq, zarb aur taqseem karna; complex numbers ko ordered pairs ki shakal mein likhna aur un ki field properties; Argand diagram aur modulus (faasla); do complex numbers ki barabari aur complex number ka square root; polynomial ko linear factors ke product mein likhna aur completing the square se quadratic equation hal karna; unity ke cube roots aur fourth roots; polar form aur polar form mein operations; aur kuch real-world istemaal (bijli ke circuits aur cryptography ka ek saada idea).
Yeh kyun zaroori hai: complex numbers ke saath har quadratic equation ke roots milte hain, degree \(n\) wale har polynomial ke poore \(n\) roots hote hain (dohraye gaye roots gin kar), aur rotation aur waves ko saada algebra se hal kiya ja sakta hai.
Pehle se kya aana chahiye: real numbers aur un ki properties; brackets kholna aur identities jaise \((a+b)^2\) aur \((a-b)(a+b) = a^2 - b^2\); saada aur quadratic equations hal karna; coordinate plane par points lagana; Pythagoras theorem; aur baad mein polar form ke liye trigonometric ratios (sin, cos, tan). Agar in mein se koi cheez kamzor hai to pehle use dohra lijiye; is unit mein yeh baar baar kaam aayengi.
Kahan kaam aata hai: electrical engineering (alternating current, voltage aur impedance), signal aur image processing, control systems, physics (waves, quantum mechanics), computer graphics, aur aage ki mathematics mein jahan bhi polynomial equations hal hoti hain.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Complex number ki shakal \(z = a + ib\) hai, jahan \(a\) aur \(b\) dono real numbers hain.
2. \(i = \sqrt{-1}\), is liye \(i^2 = -1\). Yeh ek fact poori unit ki chaabi hai.
3. Tamam complex numbers ke set ko \(C\) kehte hain.
4. Complex numbers is liye banaye gaye ke real numbers mein negative number ka square root mojood nahi.
5. \(a\) aur \(b\) ke sign hamesha un ke saath jate hain: \(-7 - 2i\) mein \(a = -7\), \(b = -2\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
Bohat se students \(i = -1\) likh dete hain. Yeh ghalat hai! \(i = \sqrt{-1}\) hai; \(-1\) to \(i^2\) ke barabar hai. Farq yaad rakhne ka asaan tareeqa: \(i\) khud \(\sqrt{-1}\) hai, aur jab \(i\) ko \(i\) se zarb dein tab \(-1\) milta hai.
Yeh samajhna ke \(a + ib\) mein \(b\) hamesha positive hoga. \(-7 - 2i\) mein \(b = -2\) hai, aur \(2 - \frac{5}{7}i\) mein \(b = -\frac{5}{7}\).
\(b\) ke saath \(i\) bhi likh dena, jaise "\(b = 4i\)". \(b\) sirf real number hai: \(3 + 4i\) mein \(b = 4\).
